correctness.rationale: In characteristic two the polar derivatives have simultaneous projective zeros [1:t:t^5], t^7=1, all off the quartic; the 3-dimensional F2-image u->(u,u^4,u^2) identifies them as a Fano subplane of PG(2,8). A group of order 21 generated by a Singer scaling and coordinate cycle moves the representative [1:1:alpha] through 21 curve points; three coordinate vertices give 24 total, and the genus-three Serre bound equals 24. Explicit tangent restriction at the orbit representatives shows contact order three (flex); distinct flexes cannot share a tangent by Bezout. All 24 tangents avoid U, and Fano line incidence (7 three-secants, 42 one-secants, 24 nonsecants among 73 lines) proves they exhaust nonsecants. The 24 curve points lie off seven extended Fano lines, yielding precisely 2 tangents through each; other 42 points have 4, and U has 0. Independently programmed direct GF(8) projective arithmetic (irreducible polynomial x^3+x+1) gave 73 points, 24 curve points, 7 polar points, 24 tangents and incidence {0:7,2:24,4:42}, with literal nonsecant equality. This is exhaustive for F8, not a general all-fields assertion.
